web_evidence.title: Timeline - Michael Crichton
web_evidence.note: The author's official site provides three sustained passages from different situations. They narrate Johnston, Kate, Marek, and other characters externally in third person, including Kate's thoughts, with no participating narratorial frame.

web_evidence.title: Michael Crichton Writing Styles in Timeline
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies the entire novel as third-person omniscient and explains that its perspective ranges among Marek, Kate, Chris, and minor characters.

person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and narrates multiple characters externally in the third person. Several Goodreads passages provide character-specific third-person narration, including access to Marek's knowledge and another character's realization, while the official excerpts independently show the same pattern across modern and medieval scenes. First- and second-person forms in the remaining quotes are dialogue, aphorism, inclusive rhetoric, or generic hypotheticals rather than alternate base narration. The whole-book POV description confirms that the shifting character perspectives remain third-person omniscient; no material uncertainty or credible contrary structure remains.
